subject: health
unitTitle: Healthy Relationships, Consent, and Digital Boundaries
title: Mastery check: digital images and privacy
essentialQuestion: How can understanding healthy relationships, consent, and digital boundaries help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
keyPoints: Digital images can be copied or redistributed beyond the original audience; protect privacy by declining requests, not forwarding others’ images, and reporting coercion to a trusted adult.
Use observable facts, reliable information, and the appropriate support route; do not infer a person’s health, motives, or character from one detail.
For digital images and privacy, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Develop and practice age-appropriate communication, refusal, support, and reporting scripts with no personal disclosure.
studentTask: Apply the lesson facts to a supplied fictional case about digital images and privacy. Produce a three-part response that identifies the key concept, chooses a safe and feasible action, and explains the choice with two details from the instruction plus an appropriate support route.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in digital images and privacy; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the digital images and privacy task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
